rules.title: Match auto-derefs reference scrutinees
rules.statement: Matching a scrutinee of type &T, &mut T, or *T against patterns for T behaves identically to matching T directly: the reference is transparently dereferenced for enum/tuple/struct discrimination and binding (default binding modes).

rules.title: Enum match tests the discriminant
rules.statement: Matching a tagged (data-carrying) enum value loads its discriminant and dispatches arms by discriminant equality; a fieldless C-like enum value is its discriminant directly (an integer), and a reference to a fieldless enum is dereferenced to compare the discriminant rather than the pointer.

rules.title: Exhaustive discrete match needs no reachable default
rules.statement: A match whose unguarded arms cover all values of a discrete scrutinee — a bool with both true and false (or a wildcard), an enum with every variant discriminant covered (or a wildcard), or a tuple with an irrefutable arm — is exhaustive; the fall-through default branch is unreachable.

rules.title: Tuple pattern destructures by position
rules.statement: A tuple pattern is irrefutable and binds each element positionally from the tuple's inline storage, recursing per element (wildcard, scalar, nested tuple, enum-payload, or-pattern).

rules.title: Struct pattern field binding forms
rules.statement: In a struct pattern, `S { x }` binds field x under name x (shorthand); `S { x: a }` binds field x under name a (rename); both bind a struct-typed field as a place (its address, preserving mutation through the binding) and a scalar field by value.

rules.title: ref binding to a struct field
rules.statement: In a struct pattern, `S { x: ref px }` binds px to a reference to field x; for a struct-typed field px aliases the field place (so `px.f` projects through it), for a scalar field px holds the field address.

rules.title: Nested refutable sub-pattern in struct field
rules.statement: A refutable sub-pattern on a struct field (`S { x: Variant(..) }`, nested struct/tuple/or) binds its inner names recursively against the field place.

rules.title: Slice pattern over a fixed array
rules.statement: A slice pattern over an array [T; N] binds prefix elements at indices 0,1,... and suffix elements at indices N-suffix_count,...,N-1; each element binds by value (`x`) or by reference (`ref x` → pointer to element).

rules.title: Slice pattern over a dynamic slice with rest binding
rules.statement: A slice pattern over a dynamic slice &[T] binds prefix elements at offsets 0,1,...; suffix elements relative to the runtime length at len-suffix_count+i; and a named rest `xs @ ..` to a first-class sub-slice {data+prefix, len-prefix-suffix} usable for `.len()` and re-matching.

rules.title: @ pattern binds whole value and recurses
rules.statement: An `name @ subpat` pattern binds name to the whole matched value (or its place) and then binds the nested names of subpat against the same scrutinee.

rules.title: ref binding produces a reference to the scrutinee
rules.statement: A `ref name` pattern binds name to a reference (pointer) to the scrutinee place rather than moving/copying the value.

rules.title: &pat unwraps one reference level
rules.statement: A reference pattern `&pat` / `&mut pat` matches a reference scrutinee by binding the inner pattern against the referent.

rules.title: Or-pattern binds a consistent name set
rules.statement: An or-pattern `p1 | p2 | ...` binds the same set of names for every alternative; bindings are extracted from a single alternative's structure.
rules.uncertainty: Codegen extracts from the first alternative only; the requirement that all alternatives bind the same names is enforced earlier (sema), not in this unit.

rules.title: Named wildcard binds (moves) the whole scrutinee
rules.statement: A named binding pattern `name` binds the entire scrutinee: an owned struct binding aliases the scrutinee's storage (by-pointer, single drop ownership transfers, scrutinee marked moved) while a scalar/other binding takes the value.
